# Inferra

> Inferra is the Git-native cloud: an application platform that runs backends straight from a GitHub repo. A file in your repository, `.inferra/org.yaml`, defines production, staging and preview spaces, the apps (APIs, workers, containers built with buildpacks, no Dockerfile) and their managed services (Postgres, Valkey cache, S3 buckets). Installing the Inferra GitHub App and pushing to a mapped branch builds and deploys; results appear as commit statuses. Plans are flat: Free (7-day trial), Pro $20/month, Team $99/month; limits stop the next push instead of adding to the bill.

Key facts:
- Deploys only through Git pushes; the `inferra` CLI inspects and operates (logs, metrics, exec, rollback, promote) but never deploys.
- A managed database or cache accepts connections only from the apps bound to it in `org.yaml`.
- Every app on every plan runs in a gVisor sandbox. Outbound network access is the same on every plan: any public port, never private ranges or cloud metadata.
- A hosted MCP server for AI assistants (Claude, Codex, VS Code, Cursor) is coming soon: read-only troubleshooting, and configuration changes only as pull requests to `org.yaml`.
- Custom domains are coming soon.

## Pages
- [Homepage](https://inferralab.com/): product overview, plans and network rules
- [Your first deployment](https://inferralab.com/setup): Inferra builds and deploys apps from GitHub pushes. This guide connects a repository, defines its spaces and app, and shows how to read the result.
- [org.yaml reference](https://inferralab.com/docs/org-yaml): The .inferra/org.yaml file declares an Inferra repository’s spaces, branch mappings, apps and service bindings. This reference covers every field accepted by the parser.
- [CLI reference](https://inferralab.com/docs/cli): The Inferra CLI inspects repository orgs and operates running workloads. GitHub pushes deploy source; customer commands cover logs, metrics, instances, rollback and promotion.
- [Documentation](https://inferralab.com/docs): Inferra is a GitHub-native platform for APIs, workers and their data. Start with one setup guide, then use the configuration and CLI references for precise details.
- [The public demo](https://inferralab.com/demo): The Inferra demo repository will show an API, a worker and Postgres deployed from GitHub. The live demo goes live with the demo video; it is not running yet.
- [MCP is coming soon](https://inferralab.com/mcp): Inferra’s planned MCP server will let assistants read troubleshooting evidence and propose configuration changes as pull requests to org.yaml. It is not available yet.
- [Security and data handling](https://inferralab.com/security): Inferra isolates apps with gVisor, controls network access by space and service binding, and keeps secret values out of read APIs. This page describes the implemented controls and preview limits.
- [Website privacy](https://inferralab.com/privacy): The inferralab.com static website collects no analytics today. If analytics is enabled later, it will be first-party and cookieless.
- [Page not found](https://inferralab.com/404.html): This address does not point to a page on the Inferra website. Use the documentation or setup guide to find your next step.
- [Comparisons are coming soon](https://inferralab.com/compare): Inferra comparison pages are not published yet. Each future comparison will be dated and checked against its sources.
- [Release notes](https://inferralab.com/changelog): Inferra CLI release notes live with the public GitHub releases. The download page identifies the exact preview release offered by this website.
- [Download the CLI](https://inferralab.com/download): Git pushes create deployments; the CLI inspects and operates them.
